title: Communication Systems
tagline: Analog and digital modulation, noise, detection, bit error rates and wireless systems
summary: Communication systems move information across distance through noisy, band-limited channels. This course analyses analog amplitude and angle modulation, sampling and pulse-code modulation, baseband and passband digital transmission, optimal detection in noise, and the techniques used in modern wireless systems.

chapters.title: Signals, spectra and channels
chapters.summary: Bandwidth, bandpass signals and complex envelopes, the Hilbert transform and models of communication channels.

chapters.title: Amplitude modulation
chapters.summary: DSB, conventional AM, SSB and VSB modulation, envelope and coherent detection, and the superheterodyne receiver.

chapters.title: Frequency and phase modulation
chapters.summary: FM and PM, Carson’s rule, FM generation and demodulation, and the phase-locked loop.

chapters.title: Noise in analog communication
chapters.summary: Signal-to-noise ratio in AM and FM receivers, threshold effects and pre-emphasis.

chapters.title: Sampling and pulse-code modulation
chapters.summary: PCM, quantisation noise, companding, delta modulation and time-division multiplexing.

chapters.title: Baseband digital transmission
chapters.summary: Line codes, pulse shaping, intersymbol interference, the Nyquist criterion, raised-cosine pulses and eye diagrams.

chapters.title: Digital modulation
chapters.summary: ASK, FSK, PSK and QAM, signal constellations, bandwidth efficiency and orthogonal signalling.

chapters.title: Detection in noise
chapters.summary: Matched filters, maximum-likelihood detection, and the bit and symbol error rates of digital modulations.

chapters.title: Wireless communication
chapters.summary: Multipath fading, diversity, OFDM, multiple access, and link budgets of cellular and Wi-Fi systems.
